### Method reminder

For a linear function inside the denominator, $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{ax+b}=\dfrac1a\ln|ax+b|+c$: divide by the coefficient of $x$.

### Solution

$\displaystyle\int\dfrac{3}{2x+1}\,dx=3\times\dfrac12\ln|2x+1|+c=\dfrac32\ln|2x+1|+c$. Differentiating back: $\dfrac32\cdot\dfrac{2}{2x+1}=\dfrac3{2x+1}$.

$3\ln|2x+1|$ forgets the chain-rule factor $\tfrac12$, and $6\ln|2x+1|$ multiplies by $2$ instead of dividing. The option $-\dfrac{3}{(2x+1)^2}$ is the derivative, not the integral.

### Method reminder

When the numerator is (a multiple of) the derivative of the denominator, $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx=\ln|f(x)|+c$.

### Solution

Since $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^2+1)=2x$, $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x}{x^2+1}\,dx=\tfrac12\ln(x^2+1)$. Then $\tfrac12\ln2-\tfrac12\ln1=\tfrac12\ln2\approx0.347$.

$\ln2$ forgets the factor $\tfrac12$; $2\ln2$ multiplies instead; $\dfrac\pi4$ comes from treating the integrand as $\dfrac1{x^2+1}$ (the arctan integral).

### Method reminder

Split into partial fractions $\dfrac{A}{x-1}+\dfrac{B}{x+4}$, integrate each term as a logarithm, then combine with the laws of logarithms.

### Solution

$5=A(x+4)+B(x-1)$: $x=1\Rightarrow A=1$; $x=-4\Rightarrow B=-1$. So the integrand is $\dfrac1{x-1}-\dfrac1{x+4}$.

$\displaystyle\int_2^6=\left[\ln\dfrac{x-1}{x+4}\right]_2^6=\ln\dfrac12-\ln\dfrac16=\ln\dfrac{1/2}{1/6}=\ln3$.

$-\ln3$ reverses the limits; $5\ln3$ keeps the numerator $5$ as a factor; $-\ln2$ uses only the upper limit.

### Method reminder

When the numerator has degree greater than or equal to that of the denominator, divide first; then integrate the polynomial part and the proper fraction separately.

### Solution

$\dfrac{x^2+1}{x+1}=x-1+\dfrac{2}{x+1}$ (check: $(x+1)(x-1)+2=x^2+1$).

$\displaystyle\int_0^2\left(x-1+\dfrac2{x+1}\right)dx=\left[\tfrac{x^2}2-x+2\ln(x+1)\right]_0^2=(2-2+2\ln3)-0=2\ln3$.

$2+2\ln3$ omits the $-x$ term and $4+2\ln3$ uses $+x$; $\ln3$ forgets the factor $2$ on the log.

enonce_markdown: Express $\dfrac{3x+1}{(x+1)^{2}(x-1)}$ in partial fractions. Hence show that $\displaystyle\int_2^3\dfrac{3x+1}{(x+1)^{2}(x-1)}\,dx=\ln\dfrac32+\dfrac1{12}$.

### Method reminder

A repeated linear factor $(x+1)^2$ needs two terms, $\dfrac{B}{x+1}+\dfrac{C}{(x+1)^2}$. Find the constants by substituting convenient values and comparing coefficients. Integrate $\dfrac{1}{(x+1)^2}$ as a power, not a logarithm.

### Solution

$\dfrac{3x+1}{(x+1)^2(x-1)}=\dfrac{A}{x-1}+\dfrac{B}{x+1}+\dfrac{C}{(x+1)^2}$, so $3x+1=A(x+1)^2+B(x-1)(x+1)+C(x-1)$.

$x=1$: $4=4A\Rightarrow A=1$. $x=-1$: $-2=-2C\Rightarrow C=1$. Coefficient of $x^2$: $0=A+B\Rightarrow B=-1$. Check the coefficient of $x$: $3=2A+C=3$. Therefore

$$\dfrac{3x+1}{(x+1)^2(x-1)}=\dfrac1{x-1}-\dfrac1{x+1}+\dfrac1{(x+1)^2}.$$

$$\int_2^3\!\left(\dfrac1{x-1}-\dfrac1{x+1}+\dfrac1{(x+1)^2}\right)dx=\left[\ln(x-1)-\ln(x+1)-\dfrac1{x+1}\right]_2^3.$$

At $x=3$: $\ln2-\ln4-\tfrac14$. At $x=2$: $\ln1-\ln3-\tfrac13$. Subtracting: $\ln2-\ln4+\ln3-\tfrac14+\tfrac13=\ln\dfrac{2\times3}{4}+\tfrac1{12}=\ln\dfrac32+\dfrac1{12}$. $\blacksquare$

enonce_markdown: Express $\dfrac{3x^{2}+x+2}{x(x^{2}+1)}$ in the form $\dfrac{A}{x}+\dfrac{Bx+C}{x^{2}+1}$, and hence find the exact value of $\displaystyle\int_1^2\dfrac{3x^{2}+x+2}{x(x^{2}+1)}\,dx$.

### Method reminder

An irreducible quadratic factor needs a numerator $Bx+C$. Split $\dfrac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}$ into $\dfrac{Bx}{x^2+1}$ (a logarithm) and $\dfrac{C}{x^2+1}$ (an arctangent).

### Solution

$3x^2+x+2=A(x^2+1)+(Bx+C)x$. $x=0$: $A=2$. Coefficient of $x^2$: $3=A+B\Rightarrow B=1$. Coefficient of $x$: $1=C$. So the fraction is $\dfrac2x+\dfrac{x+1}{x^2+1}$.

$\displaystyle\int\left(\dfrac2x+\dfrac{x}{x^2+1}+\dfrac1{x^2+1}\right)dx=2\ln x+\tfrac12\ln(x^2+1)+\arctan x$.

Between $1$ and $2$: $2\ln2+\tfrac12\ln5-\tfrac12\ln2+\arctan2-\tfrac\pi4=\tfrac32\ln2+\tfrac12\ln5+\arctan2-\tfrac\pi4$.

This equals $\tfrac12\ln40+\arctan2-\dfrac\pi4\approx1.8445+1.1071-0.7854=2.166$ (numerical check agrees).
